# Feature Specification: Fixed-Time Session Slot Pre-Generation

**Feature Branch**: `018-fixed-time-slot-pregeneration`

**Created**: 2026-09-03

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: User description: "Fixed-Time Session Slot Pre-Generation — when a Fixed-Time Session is generated by the nightly job (011), every one of its bookable Slots is created in the same step, spaced by the parent Schedule's per-patient duration, each starting OPEN. A number of those Slots (per the buffer-sizing formula, 022, not yet built) are marked as buffer, spread evenly through the day rather than clustered at the end. Per build-order.md's own documented resolution for the 012↔022 circular dependency, this feature uses 022's own cold-start fallback rule (fewer than 5 no-show data points → exactly 1 buffer slot) as a hardcoded v1 behavior, via a swappable calculation seam 022 will upgrade in place once it's built and 021 exists to feed it real no-show data. Queue/Token Sessions get no Slots from this feature at all — that's 013's (not yet built) separate on-demand path. (Full source: backlog/012-fixed-time-slot-pregeneration.md)"

## Scope Decisions Made During Drafting

No prior conversation turn resolved these — they're research-backed defaults made while writing this spec, not a `/speckit-clarify` session (which runs next and may revisit any of them).

- **Buffer slot count is hardcoded to exactly 1 per Fixed-Time Session, via a named, swappable calculation seam — not a rough approximation of 022's formula.** build-order.md's own documented resolution for the 012↔022 circular dependency states this precisely: "build 012 first, using the cold-start fallback that 022's own business rules already define — minimum 5 data points, else a flat single-slot default applies... Build 022's full 90-day trailing formula afterward... and have it upgrade 012's slot-generation logic in place." Since no no-show data can possibly exist yet (021, the no-show detection feature, is also unbuilt), the "fewer than 5 data points" branch of 022's own already-written business rules always applies right now — so 1 buffer slot per session is not a guess, it's the literal, currently-unconditional value of a rule this backlog has already fully specified elsewhere.
- **A buffer slot is one of the session's own regularly-spaced time slots, tagged as buffer, not an extra slot appended beyond the time window.** "Spread evenly through the day" only makes sense read this way — the source material describes distributing buffer status *across* the day's existing slot sequence, not adding supplementary slots that would extend the clinic's hours beyond what the Schedule's own time window defines.
- **No HTTP endpoint or UI is introduced by this feature.** Every capability here (pre-generating Slots as part of session generation, and their being queryable) is consumed by future features (016/017/018/023) that don't exist yet — this feature ships as an extension of 011's existing service-layer contract (Constitution Principle III's service-interface allowance), the same "generic capability now, wiring/UI later" pattern already used repeatedly in this backlog (e.g. 011 itself, 036).
- **A `Slot`'s status is a genuinely extensible field (`SlotStatus`), defined with only its one currently-meaningful value (`OPEN`) for this feature's own scope** — not a fully speculative BOOKED/CANCELLED/NO_SHOW state machine invented ahead of the features (016/017/018/020/021/025) that will each need to add their own transition. This mirrors this backlog's established pattern of extending an existing enum/entity in place exactly when a later feature needs to (e.g. `ScheduleMode`, `NotificationEventStatus`).
- **Slot generation is added directly to 011's existing `generateForSchedule` method**, immediately after a Fixed-Time Session is saved, in the same transaction — not a separate, later pass — because the source business rule is explicit that Slots are created "in the same step" as the Session itself, and 011's per-schedule transaction is exactly the unit of work that step belongs in.

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Every Slot of a Fixed-Time Session Exists the Moment the Session Does (Priority: P1)

When the nightly (or manually re-triggered) session-generation job creates a Fixed-Time Session, every bookable Slot for that day — spaced by the doctor's configured per-patient duration, each starting OPEN — is created in that same step, with no separate pass and no slot appearing lazily later.

**Why this priority**: This is the entire reason the feature exists — a Fixed-Time clinic's whole day needs to be immediately visible and bookable end-to-end, not built up incrementally.

**Independent Test**: Generate Sessions from a Fixed-Time Schedule (9am–1pm, 15-minute slots); confirm the resulting Session has exactly the expected count of Slots, each starting OPEN, correctly spaced across the window.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a Fixed-Time Recurring Schedule configured for a 9am–1pm window with a 15-minute per-patient duration, **When** its Session is generated for a date, **Then** all 16 Slots for that window are created immediately, each in `OPEN` status.
2. **Given** a Queue/Token Recurring Schedule, **When** its Session is generated, **Then** zero Slots are created for it by this feature — that mode's Slots are a separate, not-yet-built feature's responsibility.
3. **Given** a Fixed-Time Session that has already had its Slots pre-generated, **When** generation runs again for the same (Schedule, date) pair, **Then** no duplicate Slots are created (the Session itself is already protected from duplicate generation by 011; this feature never independently re-generates Slots for an already-existing Session).

---

### User Story 2 - Buffer Slots Are Reserved and Spread Evenly, Not Clustered at the End (Priority: P2)

Of a Fixed-Time Session's pre-generated Slots, a calculated number are reserved as buffer capacity — for v1, always exactly 1 per session (022's own cold-start fallback rule, since no no-show history can exist yet) — positioned near the middle of the day's sequence rather than appended at the very end.

**Why this priority**: Buffer slots are what make walk-in insertion (020, not yet built) and other day-of slack possible — but the count and distribution logic, not the mere existence of Slots, is this story's own incremental value on top of User Story 1.

**Independent Test**: Generate a Fixed-Time Session; confirm exactly one of its Slots is marked as buffer, and that its position is at (or near) the middle of the sequence, not the last index.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a Fixed-Time Session with 16 total Slots, **When** it is generated, **Then** exactly 1 Slot is marked as buffer.
2. **Given** the same Session, **When** the buffer Slot's position is inspected, **Then** it is at (or nearest to) the middle of the sequence — never the last Slot.
3. **Given** the buffer count calculation is performed, **When** it runs, **Then** it is implemented as a named, independently-swappable component — not logic inlined directly into slot generation — so 022 can later replace its output without changing anything else about how Slots are created or positioned.

---

### Edge Cases

- What happens when a Fixed-Time Schedule's window doesn't divide evenly by its slot interval (e.g. a 50-minute window with 15-minute slots)? → The last full interval that fits is generated; a Slot is never created if it would extend past the Schedule's own end time.
- What happens when a Fixed-Time Session would produce only 1 total Slot? → That single Slot is also the buffer Slot (the only position that exists is, trivially, "the middle").
- What happens to Slots already pre-generated for a Session when its parent Schedule is later edited (014)? → Unaffected — 014's non-retroactivity guarantee already ensures an edited Schedule never touches an existing Session, and by extension never touches that Session's Slots either, since this feature's Slots reference the Session (already immutable-by-edit), not the Schedule directly.

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-001**: When a Fixed-Time Session is generated (011), system MUST create every Slot for that Session's time window in the same step (the same transaction), spaced by the parent Schedule's slot-interval duration, as recorded on the Session.
- **FR-002**: Each pre-generated Slot MUST start in `OPEN` status.
- **FR-003**: When a Queue/Token Session is generated, system MUST NOT create any Slot for it via this feature.
- **FR-004**: System MUST determine each Fixed-Time Session's buffer-slot count via a distinct, independently-replaceable component, MUST NOT create a Slot that would extend past the Session's own end time.
- **FR-005**: For v1, the buffer-slot-count component MUST always return exactly 1 for a Fixed-Time Session — the cold-start fallback 022's own (separately specified) business rules define for "fewer than 5 no-show data points," which is unconditionally the current state since no no-show data exists anywhere in this codebase yet.
- **FR-006**: System MUST mark exactly the calculated number of Slots as buffer, positioned as evenly as possible across the Session's Slot sequence — never all clustered at the final position(s).
- **FR-007**: A buffer Slot MUST be one of the Session's own regularly-spaced Slots (tagged, not additional) — pre-generation MUST NOT create any Slot beyond what the time window and interval alone would produce.

### Key Entities

- **Slot** (new entity, first defined by this feature): one bookable time unit within a Fixed-Time Session. Fields: the Session it belongs to, a start time, an end time, whether it's a buffer slot, a status (`OPEN` is this feature's only defined value), a created timestamp.
- **Session** (from 011, read-only here): supplies the time window, mode, and slot-interval this feature reads to generate Slots — never written to by this feature beyond what 011 itself already does.

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: 100% of generated Fixed-Time Sessions have exactly the Slot count their time window and interval imply, each starting `OPEN`, verified directly at the data layer.
- **SC-002**: 100% of generated Queue/Token Sessions have zero Slots created by this feature.
- **SC-003**: 100% of generated Fixed-Time Sessions have exactly 1 buffer Slot (v1's fixed cold-start value), positioned at or nearest the middle of the sequence, never the last index (except when the session has only one Slot total).
- **SC-004**: 100% of repeated generation runs over an already-generated Session produce zero additional Slots for that Session.

## Assumptions

- **No Booking/booking-attachment behavior is built or tested by this feature.** The source acceptance criterion describing a later booking attaching to an existing pre-generated Slot (rather than creating a new one) describes 016/017's own future behavior, made possible by this feature's Slots existing — not something this feature itself has any code path to exercise, since no Booking entity exists yet.
- **No dedicated "view a day's Slots" endpoint is built by this feature** — the source acceptance criterion about Slots being "visible" before any booking occurs is satisfied at the data layer (a queryable `SlotRepository`); which future feature (a booking flow, or a dedicated schedule-viewing feature) exposes that over HTTP is out of this feature's scope to decide now.
- **`BufferSlotCalculator` is a named, injectable component (not a hardcoded literal spread across the codebase)**, specifically so 022 can later provide a different implementation without touching this feature's slot-generation or even-distribution logic — this is a direct implementation of build-order.md's own stated intent ("have it upgrade 012's slot-generation logic in place").
